items.title: Centered finite differences for the zero-Dirichlet boundary-value problem
items.statement: For continuous g on [0,1] and an integer N≥1, form h=1/(N+1), the interior grid, and the centered second-difference Dirichlet system for −u''=g; solve it by an explicit Thomas recurrence in exact real arithmetic, returning invalid-mesh or linear-solve-failure when the stated checks fail.
items.strategy: Specify inputs, the grid, exact boundary closure, matrix, recurrence, outputs and failure statuses. The following local lemma proves that all pivots are positive, the system has a unique solution, and the failure branch is unreachable for admissible inputs.
items.axiom_base: No choice or additional axiom; operations are exact real arithmetic.

items.title: Discrete maximum principle and uniform inverse bound for the Dirichlet stencil
items.statement: For every N≥1 on the uniform zero-Dirichlet grid, A_h is invertible, A_h^{-1} preserves componentwise nonnegativity, and ||A_h^{-1}r||∞≤||r||∞/8 for every r∈R^N; the bound is independent of h.
items.strategy: Prove the Thomas pivots are (j+1)/j, prove the discrete maximum principle by propagation from a negative minimum, and compare A_h^{-1}r with the discrete barrier q_j=x_j(1−x_j)/2.
items.axiom_base: Choice-free finite-dimensional argument over the ordered real field.

items.title: Centered-difference residual bound with exact Dirichlet closure
items.statement: If u has four continuous derivatives on [0,1], −u''=g, and ||u⁽⁴⁾||∞≤M, then the interior centered-difference residual has max norm at most Mh²/12 and the imposed zero-Dirichlet endpoint residuals are exactly zero.
items.strategy: Apply the order-three Lagrange remainder bound at x_j−h and x_j+h for every interior node, add the two remainders, and record the exact endpoint closure residual separately.
items.axiom_base: No choice; the finite maximum norm is explicitly defined.

items.title: Second-order max-norm error for the centered Dirichlet scheme
items.statement: Under the preceding C⁴ and uniform fourth-derivative bound, the exact discrete solution has max-norm error at most Mh²/96. Any vector with residual ρ_h=A_hv_h−g_h satisfies ||v_h−u_grid||∞≤Mh²/96+||ρ_h||∞/8; this separates discretization error from linear-solve residual.
items.strategy: Set e_h=v_h−u_grid, use the exact boundary closure and residual identity A_he_h=ρ_h−τ_h, and apply the uniform inverse bound to both terms.
items.axiom_base: No choice; the proof is a finite-dimensional norm estimate over the reals.

items.title: The quadratic Dirichlet solution is represented exactly
items.statement: For g(x)=1 and u(x)=x(1−x)/2, the centered zero-Dirichlet scheme returns the exact nodal values for every N≥1.
items.strategy: Substitute the quadratic into the centered stencil, verify both endpoint values, then use the unique-solvability result.
items.axiom_base: No choice; exact algebra on a finite grid.

items.title: A first-order Neumann closure limits the global rate
items.statement: For a smooth quadratic solution of −u''=1 with left Dirichlet and right Neumann data, a first-order backward-difference closure at the right endpoint produces an exact grid error of h/2 in max norm, despite exact centered interior equations.
items.strategy: Solve the finite-difference recurrence in first differences and compare it with the exact quadratic samples; the endpoint closure defect propagates linearly across the grid.
items.axiom_base: No choice; a finite recurrence and exact arithmetic suffice.

items.title: The inverse infinity row-sum bound is uniform and sharp
items.statement: For a real matrix $B=(b_{ij})$, define its row-sum matrix norm by $\|B\|_{\mathrm{row},\infty}:=\max_i\sum_j|b_{ij}|$. For the matrices $A_h$ from [[alg-centered-difference-dirichlet-bvp]], this norm of $A_h^{-1}$ is at most $1/8$ for every $N\ge1$; at $N=3$ it is exactly $1/8$.
items.strategy: Relate the maximum row sum to the induced infinity operator norm, apply the discrete inverse estimate, then compute A_h^{-1} exactly at N=3.
items.axiom_base: No choice; row sums and the finite matrix inverse are computed exactly.
